subject: Treasury-Fed divergence over the price of money
body_md: Thesis: U.S. fiscal debt-management and monetary-policy philosophies are diverging in a way that may create a measurable signal in long-end yields, the dollar, and financing conditions. Treasury has announced that long-end liquidity-support buybacks will at least double from a $2B maximum to at least $4B per operation beginning Sep. 9, while the Fed retains formal monetary-policy authority and Reuters reports Chair Warsh favors more market price discovery as Bessent uses a more interventionist liquidity toolkit. Conviction: +0.72. Evidence: Treasury primary release https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0607/ ; Fed FOMC mandate https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomc.htm ; Reuters Aug. 27 analysis https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/bessent-warsh-diverge-who-should-set-price-money-2026-08-27/ . Contradiction: Treasury explicitly frames the operations as liquidity support, not yield targeting, and formal monetary-policy authority remains with the Fed. What would falsify this: larger buybacks have no measurable impact beyond normal liquidity improvement, or Treasury/Fed communications converge on a framework that cleanly separates liquidity support from monetary-policy signaling. Alpha-Hunter angle: compare announced/actual buybacks against intraday depth, bid-ask/liquidity, term-premium proxies, USD, mortgages and AI/data-center financing spreads; kill the extra complexity if it cannot beat a simple rates+inflation baseline.
